title: Etale-pullback naturality of the canonical quasi-coherent cohomology comparison
statement:
Let $Z$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $F_{\mathrm{et}}$ its associated small etale module [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. For $q\geq0$, let
$$c^q_{Z,F}:H^q(Z,F)\longrightarrow H^q(Z_{\mathrm{et}},F_{\mathrm{et}})$$
be the canonical comparison map, defined as follows. Both sides are computed in the categories of all structure-sheaf modules by injective resolutions, the right side being module cohomology as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison]. Write $\epsilon_{Z,*}$ for restriction of $\mathcal O_{Z,\mathrm{et}}$-modules to Zariski open subschemes, so that $\Gamma(Z,\epsilon_{Z,*}I)=\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{et}},I)$ for every $\mathcal O_{Z,\mathrm{et}}$-module $I$, and $\epsilon_{Z,*}F_{\mathrm{et}}=F$ with the identity on sections by the equivalence cited above. Then $c^q_{Z,F}$ is the map $\varphi^*$ given by the recipe of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] for the identity map $\varphi:F\to\epsilon_{Z,*}F_{\mathrm{et}}$, with the direct image $h_*$ there replaced by $\epsilon_{Z,*}$: choose injective resolutions $F_{\mathrm{et}}\to I^\bullet$ and $F\to J^\bullet$, a quasi-isomorphism $\lambda:\epsilon_{Z,*}I^\bullet\to J'^\bullet$ into a bounded below complex of injective $\mathcal O_Z$-modules, and a chain map $J^\bullet\to J'^\bullet$ under $F$; then $\Gamma(Z,\lambda)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $c^q_{Z,F}$ is the resulting map $H^q(\Gamma(Z,J^\bullet))\to H^q(\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{et}},I^\bullet))$, independent of the choices. This is the canonical map of Stacks Tag 03DW, part (2): each $c^q_{Z,F}$ is an isomorphism, $c^0_{Z,F}$ is the identity of $\Gamma(Z,F)$, and it is a canonical choice of the isomorphisms of [lem-sc-etale-zariski-qcoh-comparison]. These canonical comparisons are $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$-linear. For every etale morphism $a:Z'\to Z$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and every $q\geq0$ they satisfy
$$c^q_{Z',a^*F}\circ a^*_{\mathrm{Zar}}=a^*_{\mathrm{et}}\circ c^q_{Z,F},$$
where $a^*_{\mathrm{Zar}}:H^q(Z,F)\to H^q(Z',a^*F)$ is the cohomology pullback (a) of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], $a^*_{\mathrm{et}}$ is restriction to the etale object $Z'$ followed by the canonical identification $(a^*F)_{\mathrm{et}}\cong a_{\mathrm{et}}^*F_{\mathrm{et}}$, and $a^*F$ is tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. The equality is semilinear for the structural ring map on global sections. The comparisons also commute with every map of quasi-coherent modules on $Z$. No quasi-compactness or separatedness assumption on $Z$ or $a$ is required.

proof.text: Use the ringed morphism $\epsilon_Z$ whose direct image is restriction to open subschemes. The quasi-coherent equivalence identifies $\epsilon_{Z,*}F_{\mathrm{et}}=F$ by the identity on open sections. Work in a common universe for the sites and coefficients; module sheaves are Grothendieck abelian and therefore have enough injectives. Apply the ringed-site coefficient-map calculus to $f=\epsilon_Z$ and $\phi=\mathrm{id}_F$. Its formula is exactly the $\lambda,\beta$ roof specified in the statement, so it defines $c^q_{Z,F}$ independently of the resolutions; in particular $\Gamma(\lambda)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. It is linear over $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ and in degree zero is the identity. This application is to ringed-site module cohomology, not to constant-ring module cohomology.

source.place: 03DW, proposition-same-cohomology-quasi-coherent (2), canonical resolution map; sites-cohomology.tex derived sections and 03FD

proof.text: Choose a nonnegative injective module resolution $F_{\mathrm{et}}\to I^\bullet$ and put $K^\bullet=\epsilon_{Z,*}I^\bullet$. For every affine open $V\subseteq Z$, the associated sheaf restricted to $V_{\mathrm{et}}$ is $(F|_V)_{\mathrm{et}}$ and is quasi-coherent. The module/abelian evaluation comparison and its slice version identify $H^q(I^\bullet(V))$ with $H^q(V_{\mathrm{et}},(F|_V)_{\mathrm{et}})$. Affine etale vanishing makes this zero for $q>0$; for $q=0$ it is $F(V)$. Thus the augmented section complex $0\to F(V)\to K^0(V)\to K^1(V)\to\cdots$ is exact for every affine open $V$. Affine opens form a basis. An arbitrary local cocycle may therefore be restricted around each point to an affine open, where it is a boundary; the resulting local primitives show exactness of the augmented complex of Zariski sheaves $F\to K^\bullet$. No assertion that arbitrary intersections of affines are affine is used.

source.place: 03DW proof, paragraph beginning Choose an injective resolution, and affine vanishing preceding it

proof.text:
The direct-image acyclicity theorem, applied to $\epsilon_Z$ and each injective $I^n$, says that $K^n=\epsilon_{Z,*}I^n$ is acyclic for evaluation on every Zariski open, in particular for global sections on $Z$. Its hypotheses hold because the inclusion of opens presents the ringed-site morphism from Step 1; no structural-map flatness is needed. Hence the acyclic-resolution criterion gives the canonical isomorphism
$$d^q:H^q(\Gamma(Z,K^\bullet))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(Z,F).$$
The normalized coefficient-map calculus identifies $c^q_{Z,F}$ with $(d^q)^{-1}$, using the section identity $\Gamma(Z,K^\bullet)=\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{et}},I^\bullet)$. Consequently every $c^q_{Z,F}$ is an isomorphism. This is the inverse of the restriction-resolution map in the proof of the source proposition. The module/abelian evaluation comparison gives its interpretation in etale abelian cohomology. Its naturality in $F$ follows from coefficient naturality in the calculus and from the natural identity on open sections in the quasi-coherent equivalence; it is therefore a canonical family with the properties asserted by the existing cohomology-comparison node.

source.place: 03DW proof, restriction-resolution comparison, with sites-cohomology.tex Lemma 0733 acyclic-resolution interpretation

proof.text:
Fix an etale $a:Z'\to Z$ and put $F'=a^*F$, $E=F_{\mathrm{et}}$, $E'=F'_{\mathrm{et}}$. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence. Let $\alpha:E\to a_{\mathrm{et},*}E'$ be the transpose of the canonical comparison $a_{\mathrm{et}}^*E\simeq E'$, and let $\eta:F\to a_*F'$ be the tensor-pullback unit. Write $e:F\to\epsilon_{Z,*}E$ and $e':F'\to\epsilon_{Z',*}E'$ for the identity-on-opens maps. The underived ringed square identifies $\epsilon_{Z,*}a_{\mathrm{et},*}$ with $a_*\epsilon_{Z',*}$ and normalizes the adjoint pullback comparison by these adjunctions. Under this identification,
$$\epsilon_{Z,*}(\alpha)\circ e=a_*(e')\circ\eta.$$
Indeed on an open $W\subseteq Z$, both maps take $s\in F(W)$ to its tensor-pullback section $a^*s\in F'(a^{-1}W)$. Locally this is $1\otimes s$, with coefficients acting by $a^\sharp$; the identity-on-open-sections maps do nothing further. Equality for every $W$ proves equality of the module maps. Only the unrestricted first clause of the square theorem is used, never its quasi-compact separated direct-image clause.

The site $Z'_{\mathrm{et}}$ identifies with $Z_{\mathrm{et}}/Z'$: an object is precisely an etale $Z$-scheme factoring through $Z'$. The localized ring and $\mathcal O_{Z',\mathrm{et}}$ have the same value $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ and the same restrictions on every such object. The associated module has value $\Gamma(V,(a v)^*F)$, identified with $\Gamma(V,v^*F')$ by tensor-pullback composition. Thus $a_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the ringed localization, and $\alpha$ is its unit followed by this identification. The localization normalization of the calculus says that $T_{a_{\mathrm{et}}}^q(\alpha)$ is exactly the restriction map denoted $a^*_{\mathrm{et}}$ in the statement, including its module/abelian interpretation. The same calculus applied to the scheme's Zariski ringed-site morphism and the unit $\eta$ is the recipe of the module-cohomology-map definition, so $T_a^q(\eta)=a^*_{\mathrm{Zar}}$. These identifications specify the actual maps, not just isomorphic source and target groups.

source.place: 03LC (1) and 071N slice convention; sites-cohomology.tex localization and module cohomology

proof.text: Apply the composition rule of the calculus to the equality of coefficient maps in Step 4, using the section-preserving ringed-square comparison. The path through $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$ gives $T_{a_{\mathrm{et}}}^q(\alpha)\,T_{\epsilon_Z}^q(e)$; the path through $Z'_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ gives $T_{\epsilon_{Z'}}^q(e')\,T_a^q(\eta)$. Steps 1 and 5 identify these respectively with $a^*_{\mathrm{et}}c^q_{Z,F}$ and $c^q_{Z',F'}a^*_{\mathrm{Zar}}$, proving the required equality. The coefficient maps are linear for the structural maps of ring sheaves, so the calculus makes both composites semilinear over $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)\to\Gamma(Z',\mathcal O_{Z'})$. The proof used affine opens only around individual points, injective resolutions in all module sheaves, and the unrestricted ringed square. It therefore imposes no quasi-compactness or separatedness condition on $Z$ or $a$.

The item's statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to clones/live and side-live; live is still unsplit, there is no repair note and no SGA citation. Step 1: the calculus applied to epsilon with phi = id gives exactly the stated lambda/beta roof, with c^0 = id and linearity. Step 2: on each affine V, I(V) computes the module evaluation cohomology, the slice and localization nodes take it to V_et with (F|_V)_et quasi-coherent, and affine etale vanishing applies; the affine basis gives local exactness without assuming affine intersections. Step 3: the ringed-site direct-image acyclicity node plus Leray (2) give d^q, the calculus's acyclic-resolution clause gives c = (d^q)^{-1}, and naturality in F comes from the composition rule with f = id or g = id. Step 4: the first clause of the square node is the identity on sections and its comparison is the unit/counit mate, so eps_*(alpha) e = a_*(e') eta is the conjugate identity; the equivalence node's comparison is proved from this square node, so the two agree. Step 5: Z'_et is the slice Z_et/Z', so T(alpha) is restriction by the localization clause, and the Zariski roof equals the def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap recipe (a). Step 6: composition along both paths plus the 2-isomorphism clause gives the equation. New node: self-contained, every notion cites its definition node, statement-only, searched with leansearch/leanfinder/loogle/grep. Tested on f = id, a non-flat ring map Z -> Z/2 on the point, q = 0 and the empty site. Gamma(Y,f_*I) = Gamma(X,I) and the quasi-isomorphism of Gamma(lambda) hold by 072Z; I found no false clause. Not a duplicate of the ringed-site Leray spectral sequence, triple-resolution formulas, Cech coefficient comparison, Cech refinement square or the scheme-only fmap nodes, and not a restatement of the item. Accepted, as are the 13 declared tool_uses. No changes.
